quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the traffic lane.
Pump the brakes repeatedly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, stay calm. Hold the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the gas to let the car slow down. Brake lightly once the car has slowed enough. Do not move to the shoulder until your car has slowed down considerably.

questions.question: If the rear of your car starts skidding to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Lightly tap the brakes and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car starts to skid, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This brings the front of the car in line with the rear and straightens out your vehicle.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what should you do?

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: When merging, look for a gap large enough to safely enter the flow of traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there are no safe gaps to merge into.

questions.question: How can you identify an aggressive driver?

options.text: They make sudden, unsafe lane changes.
The number of passengers in their car.
They drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make sudden, unsafe lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch the drivers around you. If you see someone making sudden or unsafe lane changes, do not challenge them. The safest thing to do is stay away from an aggressive driver.

questions.question: When must you obey instructions from school crossing guards?

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Only when you see children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always obey the instructions of school crossing guards near schools.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A downward-pointing triangle is always a yield sign. You must be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: In Arkansas, what can shared center lanes be used for?

options.text: To turn left.
To merge into a traffic lane after making a left turn.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A shared center turn lane has a solid yellow line on one side and a dashed yellow line on the other. Drivers in either direction can use it to turn left or to merge into traffic after turning left from a street or driveway. You cannot use it as a speed-up lane.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped to load or unload children, what must you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop until all children have left the bus.
Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, you must stop completely. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn before moving. Even after the bus starts moving, do not proceed until you are sure no children are crossing the road.

questions.question: When is it most important to be careful when turning or stopping in rain?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
Half an hour after the rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars has not yet washed away and mixes with rain to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of the road mean about passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double yellow line means no one can cross it to pass, no matter which direction they are traveling.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes.
When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If your lane has a green arrow and the way is clear, you can go in the direction of the arrow. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with another signal.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
Immediately to the left of the cab.
Both immediately to the left of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both immediately to the left of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have much larger blind spots than cars. The driver cannot see your vehicle behind them, and you cannot see traffic ahead if you are following too closely. If you cannot see the driver's face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign alerts drivers to watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: You must use your low beams when you are:

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water droplets and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly to get back to your lane safely. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle on the left, it is safe to move back into the right lane when:

options.text: About three seconds have passed.
You can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
You can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to the right lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is turning right and you also need to turn right, you should:

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus turns.
Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn.
questions.explanation: Do not squeeze between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.

questions.question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with flashing red lights must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is pulled in.
The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm extended, you must stay stopped. You can only move when the lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled in, and the bus starts moving.

questions.question: Pressing the brake hard on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels, causing you to lose steering.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, causing you to lose steering.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels and make you lose steering control. Slow down to avoid needing hard braking.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Speed up to reach your destination faster.
Turn up the radio volume.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of fatigue: struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting from your lane, or turning up the radio. If you notice these signs, park safely and rest.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow, the best way to let other drivers see you is to turn on:

options.text: Your dashboard lights.
Your parking lights.
Your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you cannot see other vehicles or when others cannot see you. Use low beam headlights whenever you need windshield wipers.

questions.question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk straight, it is safe to drive.
Driving is not impaired if you are below the legal alcohol limit.
Alcohol impairs judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol impairs judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment is needed to respond safely to road situations. Any amount of alcohol can impair your driving ability, even below the legal limit.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street:

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle.
To keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Watch for traffic changes on the freeway. Look for signals from other drivers. Be ready for vehicles merging at on-ramps and sudden changes in road conditions.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You can turn in that direction after a complete stop.
You can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you cannot go in that direction. Stop and wait for a green signal before you proceed.
